audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE is not a post-FanDuel run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $28.9m six-month 2026 market-access revenue decline; treating the entire amount as an OE reduction computes to approximately $406m or $5.39/share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE includes higher pre-amendment market-access revenue for part of 2025, so mechanically growing it carries excess high-margin revenue into forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As such, the lower market access fees we now receive from the new agreements entered into during the third quarter of 2025 had an unfavorable impact on online margins as compared to the prior year, and we expect these lower margins to continue and further dilute with a full year of lower market access fee revenues.
audit_findings.explanation: The run-rate mismatch is demonstrated, not merely possible. However, the filed post-change scale does not change the valuation conclusion: even conservatively treating the full pre-tax $28.9m decline as an after-tax OE reduction lowers BASE value from $93.75 to about $88.36, still above the $78.02 price, while the stock remains above the reduced buy-below level.
audit_findings.action: Recast FY2025 with the actual fixed-fee schedules, terminated agreements and Boyd sportsbook costs; revisit materiality if the documented twelve-month OE reduction exceeds the filed $28.9m comparison.

audit_findings.title: Norfolk VIE funding and common-equity economics may not match
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed project expenditures are approximately $750.0m in aggregate, including an expected $300.0m during 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The common-share OE forecast and valuation perimeter must allocate Norfolk operating benefits, losses and development funding according to Boyd common's contractual economics rather than accounting consolidation alone.
audit_findings.evidence: Through the Norfolk Management Agreement, the Company is responsible for funding any operational losses and is entitled to significant economic benefits from the developed casino’s operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The asymmetry is unresolved, but the project is large enough to be material: $750.0m equals about 10.6% of the $7.058bn BASE equity value and exceeds the $479.3m annual OE anchor. Boyd exercised its ownership option in June 2026, yet the supplied filings still do not disclose the purchased percentage, price or residual waterfall. Funding could depress common OE while benefits allocated elsewhere could make consolidated projections overstate value; excluding legitimate common benefits could understate it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the option exercise documents, ownership percentage and price, development-funding and loss-sharing terms, management-fee waterfall, distributions and residual ownership; rerun OE and the valuation using Boyd common's attributable economics only.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may classify required liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum $323.613m, equal to approximately $4.30/share or 4.6% of BASE equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations, taxes, regulation or committed construction must be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added as a separable asset.
audit_findings.evidence: Our working capital deficit at December 31, 2025 and 2024 was $448.5 million and $61.2 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the cash is excess remains unresolved, but the maximum valuation effect is bounded by the entire $323.613m bridge addition. Removing all of it lowers BASE value from $93.75 to about $89.45, still above the $78.02 price, and leaves the stock above the reduced buy-below level. The latest filed working-capital deficit was $141.0m at June 2026, versus $448.5m at December 2025 after the tax-credit liability drove the year-end deficit.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 balance to operating cash, current claims, regulatory and restricted requirements, Norfolk and other committed spending, and debt-funded cash; rerun the bridge with only the documented excess amount.

audit_findings.title: A potentially nonrecurring tax-credit benefit may remain in anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $24.790m 2025 renewable-energy-credit tax benefit; full removal computes to approximately $348m or $4.63/share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in anchor OE without a sustainable recurring program, the tax-credit purchase discount is capitalized through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Pursuant to provisions under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, the Company entered into agreements to purchase $400.9 million of transferable federal energy tax credits during 2025 at a discount to face value, which resulted in an income tax benefit recorded during the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in the OE ledger is not demonstrated, and the 2026 filing describes ongoing purchases, so nonrecurrence is also unresolved. Even assuming the entire filed $24.790m benefit remains in OE and is removed, BASE value falls only to about $89.12, still above the $78.02 price, while the stock remains above the reduced buy-below level.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE adjustment ledger and credit-purchase agreements; remove the $24.790m if included and unsupported as recurring, or document sustainable purchasing volume and discounts.

audit_findings.title: Triple-net lease obligations may exceed modeled maintenance reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed context is $113.8m of 2025 master-lease rent and approximately $250m of annual company-wide maintenance capital requirements
audit_findings.mechanism: Contractual repair and minimum-investment spending above the modeled maintenance-capex allowance would reduce recurring OE; rent escalators also reduce forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The Master Leases also include substantial additional obligations that may require future uses of free cash flow, including obligations to maintain and repair the properties and minimum annual capital investment requirements.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations are current contractual requirements, not merely forward-looking risks, but the supplied record does not quantify the lease minimums or show their overlap with the $250m maintenance allowance. A recurring OE shortfall of approximately $84.3m would be sufficient to reduce BASE value to the $78.02 market price, so materiality cannot be resolved without the lease schedules.
audit_findings.action: Extract each lease's annual minimum-capital formula, repair obligations and rent escalators; reconcile them property by property to modeled maintenance capex and rerun OE for any uncovered recurring shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Repeated impairments challenge any mechanical noncash normalization
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed impairments of $128.4m in 2025, $10.5m in 2024 and $107.8m in 2023, totaling $246.7m; a full $128.4m 2025-anchor treatment swing computes mechanically to approximately $1.80bn or $23.95/share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding impairments back without recognizing associated capital destruction or replacement spending overstates OE; retaining an exceptional impairment as a recurring cash cost can understate normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Impairment charges of $128.4 million, $10.5 million and $107.8 million were recorded as a result of our 2025, 2024 and 2023 impairment tests and triggering event reviews, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Three consecutive impairment years are demonstrated, but an OE treatment error is not established because the adjustment ledger is absent. The potential scale is material: a mechanical full-gross 2025 treatment swing would move BASE value by about $23.95/share, enough to cross the $78.02 market price. That sensitivity is not itself a proposed correction because tax effects, asset closures and overlap with maintenance capex must first be traced.
audit_findings.action: Tie every annual impairment to the OE ledger, affected assets, historical capital spending, closures and the maintenance-capex allowance; rerun each scenario after retaining only economically justified add-backs or corresponding reinvestment charges.
